  - Rural architecture references (e.g. Wikipedia: Farmhouse, Hallenhaus; Fachwerkhaus) (typical footprint and ridge height)

  - Rural architecture references (e.g. Wikipedia: Barn) (typical footprint and ridge height)

  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arch_bridge (general bridge type only, no typical road-bridge dimensions)

  - Rural construction practice; typical post-and-rail fence (Wikipedia: Fence) (post spacing and fence height)

  - Agricultural history references (e.g. Wikipedia: Haystack) (typical size of a period loose haystack/rick)

- `fort_trench_section`
  - US Army FM 5-15 Field Fortifications (14 Feb 1944), para. 48b and fig. 40 (printed pp. 81-83) (standard trench 4 ft wide at top, 2 ft at bottom, 5.5 ft deep, built in short irregular sections, spoil parapet 3 ft wide each side)
  - US Army FM 5-15 (1944), para. 32 and fig. 17 (pp. 48-49) (one-man foxhole 2 ft x 3.5 ft, 4-5 ft deep, for comparison)
- `fort_sandbag_position`
  - US Army FM 5-15 Field Fortifications (1944), para. 26 (p. 45) (breastworks/parapets at least 3 ft thick at the top (protection against .30 bullets))
  - US Army FM 5-15 (1944), para. 24 (p. 38) (standard filled sandbag about 4.75 x 10 x 19 in)
  - US Army FM 5-15 (1944), para. 39 and figs. 24-25 (pp. 57-59) (light MG horseshoe emplacement: parapet 3 ft thick, chest-high gun platform, trench about 2 ft wide)
- `fort_hedgehog`
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_hedgehog (angle beams L 140/140/13 mm, about 1.8 m (original) to 2.1 m (later) long, about 198-240 kg; overall height not stated)
- `fort_barbed_wire`
  - TM-E 30-451 Handbook on German Military Forces (1945), ch. V sec. II para. 7c (double-apron fence 4 to 5 feet high (middle 4.5 ft = 1372 mm, rounded to 1400))
  - War Department MIS Special Series No. 15, German Coastal Defenses (15 Jun 1943), sec. III item 10b(2) (apron fences 4-5 ft high, up to 30 ft wide)
  - https://tpub.com/seabee/5-2.htm (US Navy Seabee manual, derived from FM 5-30 practice) (double-apron fence 4-and-2 pace and 6-and-3 pace types; anchor pickets 2 paces each side of the centre line)
